newsitem.title: USA: Tornado tosses trucks, injures six in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Tornado tosses trucks, injures six in Texas.

text.p: A powerful tornado, packing baseball-sized hail and torrential rain, battered northwest Texas on Wednesday, injuring at least six people as it tossed trailers and cars into the air.
Police said the tornado measured at least half-mile across and ripped through open land and over a highway near Shamrock on the eastern edge of the Texas Panhandle.

"We have an awful lot of damage, a lot of trucks and cars were damaged and there were some homes destroyed," a police spokeswoman said. She said at least six people were hospitalized but were not in critical condition.
Truck drivers said the tornado tore into their path as they drove along Interstate 40, throwing vehicles around like toys.

"The rain began to pick up and the next thing I know the mirror on the side of my truck flew off. Then I went tumbling and wound up over there," said Mark Davis, pointing at his battered truck which lay on its side in a ditch.
Two smaller tornadoes touched down in the area Wednesday evening but no injuries were reported. Tornado watches were posted across much of the Texas Panhandle and southwest Oklahoma.
Two weeks ago, 27 people were killed when a huge tornado wrecked dozens of homes in the central Texas town of Jarrell.
